scope.reference: user-supplied local Open Agent Builder source tree (external, non-runtime, not packaged)
scope.reference_use: Read-only behavioral and interaction comparison. No reference source is copied into Pacify-X.
scope.reference_license_observed: README declares MIT; no standalone LICENSE file was present in the supplied tree.

summary: PX has the stronger authority, immutable revision, admission, test, and owned-harness runtime, but Agent Studio exposes that model as a raw JSON textarea. The visual workflow reference demonstrates useful composition and inspector patterns without supplying PX governance.

findings.finding: Agent Studio has no structured editor even though Workflow Studio and Skill Studio do.
findings.interface_burden: The user must understand and edit the complete AgentSpec, EffectGrant, and CapabilityBinding JSON shapes at once.
findings.proposed_seam: Add normalizeAgent and validateAgent to the existing Studio editor module, and render a governed visual Agent Builder as an exact projection of the canonical payload.
findings.deletion_test: Removing the proposed seam leaves Agent Studio as the current raw textarea and reproduces the usability defect.
findings.blast_radius: Dashboard webview only; canonical backend models and authority remain unchanged.

findings.finding: Identity, instructions, harness, required tests, bindings, grants, effects, scope, cost, egress, credentials, and lifecycle boundaries are not visually separated.
findings.interface_burden: Authority-bearing fields are mixed with descriptive fields, increasing accidental authority drift and malformed candidate risk.
findings.proposed_seam: Use separate Identity, Behavior, Capabilities, Authority, Tests, and Canonical Preview panels with continuously visible preflight results.
findings.reference_pattern: Focused node inspector, model/tool configuration, and preview panels.
findings.px_adaptation: Treat harness/model and capabilities as declared bindings only; never infer credentials, provider authority, admission, or execution.
proof: MS+Enterprise identifiers fail closed in the standard builder

findings.finding: Agent candidates have no live structural validation before Save.
findings.interface_burden: Malformed identities, versions, empty instructions/tests, mismatched subjects, unbound grants, permissive policy gaps, and duplicate identifiers are discovered only after host submission.
findings.proposed_seam: Mirror backend invariants in conservative browser preflight while retaining backend validation as authority.
findings.contrary_evidence: Browser validation cannot certify runtime admission or replace Python model validation.

findings.finding: There is no bounded add/remove/edit interaction for tests, capability bindings, or effect grants.
findings.proposed_seam: Provide accessible collection editors with safe defaults, deterministic identifiers, linked subject updates, and explicit removal.
findings.px_adaptation: No drag-and-drop dependency is required; keyboard-operable controls remain first class.

findings.finding: The standard Agent Studio does not explicitly prevent Microsoft/vendor or enterprise-restricted capability bleed.
findings.proposed_seam: Declare the builder domain as px-standard and reject enterprise/vendor namespaces unless a separately governed domain-specific flow is used.

findings.finding: Canonical JSON has no governed round-trip path for Agent Studio.
findings.proposed_seam: Synchronize visual-to-JSON and JSON-to-visual representations through normalizeAgent, preserving unknown non-authority metadata while validating canonical fields.
findings.risk: A lossy normalizer could silently mutate an immutable candidate.

ranking.reason: Highest leverage and local to the existing editor seam.
Makes authority and domain separation visible before candidate creation.
Completes efficient composition and auditable canonical synchronization.

repair_evidence.css_governance: 157 duplicate selectors; 193 duplicate occurrences; 0 cross-file duplicates; contrast gate passed
repair_evidence.status_note: Implemented and section-validated; independent audit acceptance remains separate.

certification_boundary: Source repair does not imply admission, installed-host identity, full certification, or independent auditor acceptance.
